title: Omega 3: Benefits, effect on Cholesterol | Novogenia
abstract:
## What are omega-3 fatty acids?  
Omega-3 is a group of **polyunsaturated fatty acids**. They are essential nutrients. The body is therefore entirely dependent on a regular **dietary intake.** There are several types of omega-3 fatty acids.  
The three most important **types for humans** are:  
1. **Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)**is particularly found in oily fish. It is an important component of cell membranes and makes up the majority of omega-3 fatty acids in the retina and brain.  
<!--THE END-->  
1. **Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA)**is also found in fatty sea fish. This omega-3 fatty acid is important, among other things, as a starting material from which the body forms eicosanoids and DHA.  
<!--THE END-->  
1. **Alpha-linolenic acid (ALA)**is found in plants. The body can convert this omega-3 fatty acid into docosahexaenoic acid and eicosapentaenoic acid. This is especially relevant for people who don’t eat fish.
